Fixes long waits after startup and bad low-ball estimates after a cold restart or missing mempool.dat, which real wallet/Lightning integrations have hit in production.

result.summary: This PR changes estimatesmartfee's combined mode to fall back to the block-policy fee rate estimate whenever the mempool fee estimator cannot produce one (insufficient data, low coverage, or a startup/cold-restart warmup period), rather than returning an error or silently underbidding at the minimum relay fee. It adds a 144-block warmup after a fresh start or a failed mempool reload, notifies the fee estimator manager from init.cpp when mempool loading fails, and restructures the mempool estimator's internal failure handling into a typed MempoolEstimationFailure enum. About 60% of the diff is new unit and functional tests covering these fallback paths.
result.problem: Users of estimatesmartfee (default fee_rate_estimator=none) can wait up to an hour for any fee estimate after a fresh start, and after a cold restart (persistence off or a missing/corrupt mempool.dat) the estimator can silently return the minimum relay fee even though the lost mempool may have held much higher-fee transactions, causing wallets to underpay. This affects any application relying on Bitcoin Core's fee estimates, including Lightning implementations, one of whose developers reported hitting exactly this problem.

open_concerns: davidgumberg asked (2026-09-16) why the warmup end-height needs to be persisted across restarts and why 144 blocks rather than MEMPOOL_HEALTH_WINDOW_BLOCKS (6) was chosen; not yet answered as of the latest activity.

willcl-ark raised whether LOW_COVERAGE should also fall back to block_policy in combined mode and a possible odd transition between INSUFFICIENT_DATA and LOW_COVERAGE outcomes; author force-pushed a fix addressing this (2026-09-15) and confirmed the fix in a follow-up comment.
resolved_concerns: polespinasa's early API/naming nits (IsReady/IsNotReady helper, error message typo, doc wording) were all taken and fixed by the author.
davidgumberg and pseudoramdom's suggestion to use util::Expected<void,...> instead of std::optional for the health check was adopted.
jeanpablojp's concern about stale release notes/test comments describing old behavior was fixed.

Debate between keeping 3 vs clearing all mined-block stats after a failed reload (davidgumberg, willcl-ark) was resolved by the author implementing both a clear-and-warmup approach with empirical mainnet data to justify the design.

result.card: This PR makes Bitcoin Core's estimatesmartfee fall back to the block-policy fee estimate whenever the mempool fee estimator isn't ready (during initial data-gathering after startup or after a cold restart with a missing/corrupt mempool.dat), instead of returning an error or silently underbidding at the minimum relay fee. The problem is real: an LDK developer reported hitting exactly this issue in production, confirmed by a maintainer during review ('got a report from LDK dev this is happening, where block estimates are working but mempool is not' - instagibbs). The PR underwent extensive design iteration (7 force-pushes) over warmup length and whether to retain old mined-block statistics after a failed mempool reload, backed by empirical mainnet measurements from the author, and has one full ACK on the latest revision plus several concept ACKs with no standing objections. It is ready for review now; a couple of clarifying design questions from davidgumberg posted most recently remain unanswered but are not flagged as blocking. It supersedes the closed alternative PR #36095.
